'''Myron Gardner''' (born May 21, 2001)<ref>{{cite web|title=Myron Gardner – College Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/myron-gardner-1.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref> is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]], the [[South Plains College|South Plains Texans]] and the [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Little Rock Trojans]].

==High school career==
Gardner initially attended [[Loyola High School (Detroit)|Loyola High]] at [[Detroit|Detroit, Michigan]], before transferring to SPIRE Academy in [[Geneva, Ohio]], where he averaged 18 points, finishing third on the team and was ranked 283rd nationally by 247Sports.com.<ref name="GeorgetownBio">{{cite web|title=Myron Gardner – MEN'S BASKETBALL|url=https://hoyabasketball.com/players/m_gardner.htm|website=HoyaBasketball.com|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Gardner began his college career at [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], where he played in eight of the first nine games of the 2019–20 season, averaging 3.1 points per game and after being accused in a civil complaint by a Georgetown student of assault and burglary, he transferred to [[South Plains College|South Plains]]<ref name="GeorgetownBio" /> where he averaged 13.8 points and 7.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Myron Gardner – MEN'S BASKETBALL|url=https://lrtrojans.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/myron-gardner/7100|website=LRTrojans.com|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref> After a thorough investigation of the complaint, no evidence was found to warrant any charges. The complaint is considered unfounded and has been closed.

After one year at South Plains, Gardner transferred to [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Little Rock]], where he averaged 13.2 points, 9.1, rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.2 steals in 30.8 minutes as a senior. He was the team's leader in rebounds and steals while being second in points, assists and minutes and third in both three point (35.6%) and free throw percentage (75.5%). He also was second team All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]] after leading the OVC with 15 double-doubles, tied for the second-most in a year in program history and was tied for eighth nationally while ending the regular season ranked 16th in the nation in defensive rebounds per game with 6.97, being 24th in total rebounds with 274 and 31st in rebounds per game, ranking second in the OVC in each category.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gardner, Gordon Named Second Team All-OVC Honorees|url=https://lrtrojans.com/news/2023/2/28/mens-basketball-gardner-gordon-named-second-team-all-ovc-honorees.aspx|website=LRTrojans.com|date=February 28, 2023|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Osceola Magic (2023–2025)===
After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Gardner joined the [[Osceola Magic]] on November 2, 2023,<ref>{{cite web|title=Training Camp Roster Just Dropped|url=https://osceola.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-just-dropped|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref> where he played in 47 games and averaged 5.4 points, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.1 assists in 15.4 minutes.<ref name="2024ORLTC">{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Magic Sign Myron Gardner To Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/magic-myron-gardner-agree-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 11, 2024|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref>

On July 7, 2024, Gardner joined the [[Orlando Magic]] for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Nathaniel|last=Marrero|title=Tristan da Silva, Anthony Black & Jett Howard Headline Magic's Summer League Roster|url=https://www.si.com/nba/magic/news/magic-announce-summer-league-roster-01j21k59t8yf|website=SI.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref> and on September 11, he signed with the team.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Orlando Magic PR|title=PRESS RELEASE: @OrlandoMagic sign free agents Jarrett Culver, Myron Gardner, Jalen Slawson and Tre Scott #MakeItMagic|number=1834029427308589566|user=Magic_PR|date=September 11, 2024|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref><ref name="2024ORLTC" /> However, he was waived on September 19<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agents Mac McClung, Javonte Smart and Ethan Thompson|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agents-mac-mcclung-javonte-smart-ethan-thompson-20240919|website=NBA.com|date=September 19, 2024|access-date=September 20, 2024}}</ref> and eight days later, he joined the [[Osceola Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Osceola Magic Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/osceola-magic-announce-training-camp-roster/n-6160339|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2025–present)===
Gardner joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]]. On July 25, 2025, Gardner signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Heat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAT SIGN MYRON GARDNER TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT {{!}} Miami Heat |url=https://heat.com/news/heat-sign-myron-gardner-to-two-way-contract |access-date=2025-07-25 |website=heat.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 18, 2026, Gardner signed a three-year, standard contract worth $5.5 million with the Heat after averaging 11 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.3 assists, and 1.75 steals while shooting 55.2% from the field and 53.8% from the three-point line over four starts this season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAT SIGN MYRON GARDNER TO STANDARD CONTRACT {{!}} Miami Heat |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-myron-gardner-to-standard-contract#:~:text=Your%20Miami%20HEAT%20announced%20today,percent%20from%20the%20foul%20line |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=heat.com |language=en}}.</ref> On February 21, Gardner was involved in an altercation with [[Scotty Pippen Jr.]] during a 136–120 victory over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]], one which resulted in both of their ejections; the pair were ultimately fined $35,000 each for the incident.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scotty Pippen Jr., Myron Gardner fined $35,000 each for Grizzlies-Heat scuffle|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48015578/scotty-pippen-jr-myron-gardner-fined-35000-grizzlies-heat-scuffle|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>
